source: Moby-Dick, Chapter 42, The Whiteness of the Whale

annotations.note: Kingdom of Lower Burma centred on Bago, a major Southeast Asian power until Konbaung conquest in the 18th century.
Title of Burmese and Siamese kings. A white elephant was a sign of cosmic legitimacy; possessing one proved the king ruled with heaven's consent.
The name of Thailand until 1939.
The House of Hanover, rulers of Britain 1714-1901. Its heraldic device was the white horse of Saxony.
Imperial, claiming descent from the Caesars. Austrian emperors styled themselves heirs of Rome; the word carries that claim, not a medical sense.

annotations.anchor: a white stone marked a joyful day
annotations.note: Roman custom of marking a fortunate day with a white pebble, recorded by Pliny and Catullus.
Period ethnonym for Native Americans, standard in 1851 and offensive now.
Shell-bead belts used by Eastern Woodlands nations to record treaties. White signified peace and good faith; purple, war or mourning.
White winter stoat fur trimming judicial and peers' robes, worn as an emblem of unstained justice.
Zoroastrians, for whom fire is the visible icon of Ahura Mazda's purity.
Jupiter took the form of a white bull to carry off Europa. Melville compresses the myth to its colour.
The Haudenosaunee confederacy of six nations in what is now New York State and Ontario.
The Haudenosaunee midwinter ceremony sacrificed a white dog as messenger carrying the people's fidelity to the Creator.
From Latin albus, white. The full-length white linen vestment worn under the chasuble.
Period Protestant term for Roman Catholic, mildly contemptuous.
Revelation. The twenty-four elders in white before the great white throne, and the Ancient of Days whose hair is white like wool.
French for shark. Melville's derivation from requiem is a folk etymology; the true origin is uncertain.
The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, in which killing an albatross brings supernatural catastrophe. Ishmael insists he felt the dread before reading the poem.
Sailors' name for the albatross. It survives in gooney bird.
Genesis 18. Abraham bows to three visitors at Mamre without knowing what they are.
A widespread American frontier legend of an uncatchable white mustang, in print throughout the 1830s and 1840s.
Persian king who led an army so vast it was said to drink rivers dry. The horse is monarch of comparable multitudes.
The Allegheny Mountains, then the practical western boundary of American settlement.
A violent squall arriving with no dark cloud to warn of it, only white water. Feared in tropical seas for giving no notice.
Jean Froissart, whose Chronicles are the main narrative source for the Hundred Years' War and the Flemish revolts.
The Witte Kaproenen, a Ghent militia faction who killed the count's bailiff in 1379, opening the revolt against Flanders.
Revelation 6:8. The fourth horseman rides a pale horse and his name is Death.
Pentecost. The name is white Sunday, from the robes of the newly baptised.
A Carmelite, named for the white mantle worn over the brown habit.
The Norman keep at the centre of the Tower of London, whitewashed in the 13th century and named for it.
The Harz mountains of central Germany, the setting of much of the folklore the Grimms collected.
The Brocken, highest peak of the Harz, where witches were said to gather on Walpurgis Night.
To take the veil is to enter a convent. Lima's pale ruins are cast as perpetual mourning she cannot put off.
Francisco Pizarro, conqueror of the Inca and founder of Lima in 1535, which dates the city's whiteness to the conquest.
Beyond the depth a lead line can reach bottom. The sailor is in deep water and safe, whatever his eyes tell him.
A howdah is the canopied seat carried on an elephant's back. The snow sits on the Andes like one.
Contemporary slang, short for hypochondria: a fit of morbid melancholy.
2 Kings 9:30. Jezebel paints her face and adorns her head before she is thrown from the window.
Read as the chapter's thesis: whiteness terrifies because it is both the absence of colour and the sum of all colours, a blank that means everything and therefore nothing.
